raw_case_text:
A 36-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Department of the Cancer Center, complaining of fever, chills, night sweats, diarrhea, and painful oral lesions, over the past3 days. The patient had a medical history of liver transplantation8 years before, due to biliary cirrhosis, and was taking prednisone 5mg/day and mycophenolate sodium 360 mg. She also reported cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection 3 months after the transplantation, which was successfully treated with ganciclovir. The oral examination showed three well-defined shallow ulcerative lesions covered by fibrin with regular erythematous borders on the hard palate, measuring 1 cm (Figure 1A); on the vestibular and palatal gingiva between the 16 and 17 teeth measuring 0.5 cm (Figure 1B); and on the left soft palate near the uvula measuring 1.0 cm (Figure 1C).
According to the clinical findings and the previous history of CMV, the main diagnostic hypotheses were CMV reactivation or herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection. Exfoliative cytology of oral lesions was performed and an anti-CMV immunoglobulin (Ig)G test was requested. Because of the immunosuppression, ganciclovir 300mg tid was prescribed, but no improvement was observed within 7 days. Since the exfoliative cytology and the anti-CMV IgG tests were negative, the hypothesis of viral infection became less probable. A chest x-ray was normal, which ruled out lung involvement. Due to the worsening of oral lesions and the presence of gastrointestinal tract symptoms, two oral incisional biopsies:in the gingival and the palate:were taken, and a colonoscopy was performed with biopsy of a rectal lesion. The colonoscopy image showed areas with inflammatory process and eroded mucosa with an extensive ulcer measuring 2 cm on the descending colon extending to the rectum (Figure 2).
Histological sections of oral cavity biopsies revealed fragments of squamous mucosa with intense histiocytic inflammatory infiltrate associated with rounded fungal structures, which were consistent with H. capsulatum, and were confirmed by Gomori-Grocott's staining in the gum and the palate (Figure 3). Similar findings were observed in the rectal biopsy. Based on the clinical and histopathologic findings, the final diagnosis was histoplasmosis (Figure 4).
The treatment consisted of itraconazole 300 mg/day with significant improvement of local and systemic symptoms after 7 days (Figure 5). The patient was followed up for 12 months with no further lesions.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 36-year-old female liver transplant recipient presented with a 3-day history of fever, chills, night sweats, diarrhea, and painful oral ulcers.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Eight years after undergoing liver transplantation for biliary cirrhosis (maintained on prednisone and mycophenolate sodium), the patient presented to the emergency department with 3 days of fever, chills, night sweats, diarrhea, and painful oral mucosal lesions. Empiric ganciclovir (300 mg TID for 7 days) for suspected CMV reactivation produced no improvement, and her oral and gastrointestinal symptoms worsened.
subjective.past_medical_history: Liver transplantation 8 years prior for biliary cirrhosis; post-transplant CMV infection 3 months after transplant treated successfully with ganciclovir.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, night sweats, diarrhea, and painful oral ulcers. Home medications: prednisone 5 mg/day and mycophenolate sodium 360 mg.

objective.physical_examination: Intraoral exam: three well-defined shallow fibrin-covered ulcerative lesions with regular erythematous borders located on the hard palate (1.0 cm), on the vestibular and palatal gingiva between teeth 16 and 17 (0.5 cm), and on the left soft palate near the uvula (1.0 cm).
objective.routine_investigations: Oral exfoliative cytology and serum anti-CMV IgG test: negative. Chest X-ray: normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Colonoscopy: mucosal inflammation and erosion with a 2-cm ulcer extending from the descending colon to the rectum. Incisional biopsies of gingival, palatal, and rectal ulcers: squamous/colonic mucosa with intense histiocytic inflammatory infiltrate containing rounded intracellular fungal structures confirmed by Gomori-Grocott methenamine silver (GMS) staining.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated mucocutaneous (oral) and gastrointestinal (colorectal) histoplasmosis in a liver transplant recipient (CMV reactivation and HSV ruled out). Confirmation: Histopathology and Gomori-Grocott silver staining of gingival, palatal, and rectal biopsies demonstrating characteristic rounded intracellular yeast forms of Histoplasma capsulatum. Plan & clinical course: Treated with oral itraconazole 300 mg/day, achieving marked improvement of oral and systemic symptoms within 7 days and complete remission with no recurrence over 12 months of follow-up.
